Interned Enemy Aliens Tribunal
Category 19.
A.C. 424
Report: 490

REPORT

The Tribunal has had under consideration the application for the release from internment of:-

LOEWENHEIM, Walter
H.O. Ref. L.3027.

The Tribunal (Panel A) has the honour to submit the following report:-

Walter Loewenheim is a German Jew who when released from military service after the war of 1914-1918 came under the influence of the radical movement of that time and joined the "Free Socialist Youth". Shortly afterwards he joined the German Communist Party but soon became dissatisfied with it. He was expelled from the Communist Party in 1927 and became a member of the German Social Democratic Party. At an early stage he became alarmed at the progress of the movement in favour of Nazism and for the next few years devoted himself with increasing determination to the work of organizing the various labour and socialist groups and units into one coherent body to oppose the Nazis and the Communists. For this purpose he wrote the pamphlet "Socialism's New Start" under the pseudonym Miles; this pamphlet was the foundation of the "Neu Beginnen" movement in Germany. Editions of this pamphlet were published in many foreign countries, including the United Kingdom and the United States of America; the English edition was published by the N.C.L.C., the educational organization of the Trades Union Council.

Walter Loewenheim with the aid of his brother Ernest and of his friends carried on an active underground struggle against the Nazis for some years but ultimately was obliged to leave Germany in 1935. He came to this country in 1936, his intention being to participate in the exploitation of a patent belonging to Bruno Korthauser (A.C.434) relating to dampers for flues, and thereby to acquire the means to live and to carry on his struggle against the Nazis.

Since he came to the United Kingdom Walter Loewenheim has not taken part in the "Neu Beginnen" movement which is now carried on in this country by other people, but the Tribunal is satisfied that Walter Loewenheim's views are unchanged and that he is still the determined opponent of Nazism in all its forms.

The Tribunal is satisfied that Walter Loewenheim fulfils the conditions laid down in paragraph 10 of the White Paper (Cmd. 6233) and that he is actively friendly to the Allied cause.

M.I.5 has submitted a report saying that on the evidence now before it it regards the release of the brothers Loewenheim as most undesirable. A copy of the report is annexed. The view of M.I.5 is founded on the belief that Loewenheim is a determined Communist. A study of the report shows that it is based on information which is inconsistent with that obtained by the Tribunal. That Walter Loewenheim was at one time a member of the German Communist Party is true; he admits it; but the statement that "once a G.P.U. man always a G.P.U. man" is unwound. The Tribunal can see reason to doubt the sincerity of Loewenheim's change of view.
